skill.name: playwright-stealth-verify
skill.description: Check whether a Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium or CDP-driven browser presents a coherent fingerprint, using liarjs as a library against a Page you already have - navigator.webdriver, HeadlessChrome tokens, worker versus main-thread identity, patched-API integrity, WebGL versus WebGPU GPU identity. Use when asked whether an automated browser looks like a normal one, when a headless setup or a stealth plugin's effect needs measuring rather than assuming, or when an assertion on fingerprint quality belongs in a test suite.
skill.summary: Measure browser fingerprint consistency in an existing automation harness.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: The 32 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, fenced examples, and CLI documentation in SKILL.md. The loopback CDP URLs and documentation URL are expected examples, while the default network telemetry is a confirmed medium-risk privacy concern because it sends fingerprint and connection metadata to a hosted endpoint.

remediation.issue: The default online mode sends IP, ASN, HTTP, TLS, ClientHello, and header metadata to a hosted endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Make offline mode the default for automated use, require explicit consent for hosted telemetry, and document the collected fields and retention policy.

remediation.issue: A user-provided endpoint can receive browser fingerprint telemetry.
remediation.suggestion: Require an approved HTTPS endpoint in production, validate endpoint configuration, and warn before sending data outside the users infrastructure.

remediation.issue: The CDP example attaches to a running browser endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the endpoint bound to loopback, require user confirmation, and warn that exposed CDP ports can grant full browser control.

content.value_statement: Automation teams need evidence that browser identity remains internally consistent across JavaScript, workers, and graphics APIs. This skill measures an existing browser harness and turns mismatches into testable checks without modifying the browser.
actual_capabilities: Measures browser fingerprint consistency through an existing Page-like object.
Checks webdriver, headless user-agent, viewport, worker, and native API signals.
Compares WebGL and WebGPU GPU identity after browser configuration changes.
Reports client, server, score, label, checks, and schema metadata.
Connects to a user-owned browser through a local CDP endpoint.
Supports offline checks and configurable telemetry endpoints.
limitations: It measures browser signals but does not modify, hide, or repair them.
Online mode can send network and fingerprint metadata to an endpoint.
Results describe one browser environment and do not prove general anonymity.
The skill requires Node 22 or newer and an existing browser harness for Page checks.

use_cases.title: Validate a Playwright launch
use_cases.description: Run fingerprint checks after changing launch flags, proxies, or stealth plugins, then identify inconsistent browser signals.

use_cases.title: Audit a managed browser fleet
use_cases.description: Attach to an approved local CDP session and compare browser identity signals across machines or build variants.

use_cases.title: Add a fingerprint regression gate
use_cases.description: Assert a minimum score or zero bad checks in continuous integration when browser versions or automation code change.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use playwright-stealth-verify with my existing Playwright page. Explain the score, label, and any failed checks in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Compare launch settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Measure this Playwright page before and after my launch flag changes. Identify which fingerprint checks changed and explain likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an assertion
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test assertion for this browser harness that fails when critical fingerprint checks are bad or the score falls below my chosen threshold.

prompt_templates.title: Review privacy controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production browser fingerprint audit using offline mode or a self-hosted endpoint. List the data flow, consent checks, and CI failure conditions.

output_examples.input: A Playwright page returns a low score with failures for webdriver and worker consistency.
output_examples.output: The browser exposes automation through webdriver, and the worker context disagrees with the main page. Review driver configuration and ensure overrides apply consistently.

output_examples.input: A team requests an audit that must not contact external services.
output: Run the audit with offline mode.
Confirm that the test environment blocks unexpected outbound requests.

output_examples.input: A browser reports different WebGL and WebGPU GPU names.
output_examples.output: The GPU identity is inconsistent after a graphics-related configuration change. Treat the gpu-triad check as a focused regression signal.

best_practices: Use a browser and page that the user owns or has explicitly approved.
Use offline mode when external telemetry is unnecessary.
Assert on named checks as well as a score when the failure must be actionable.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to conceal automation or bypass access controls.
Do not scan pages or browsers that the user does not own.
Do not treat a passing score as proof of anonymity, safety, or policy compliance.

faq.question: What does this skill measure?
faq.answer: It measures whether browser identity signals agree across JavaScript, workers, browser properties, codecs, and graphics APIs.

faq.question: Does it make a browser stealthy?
faq.answer: No. It reports inconsistencies and does not patch browser APIs, change launch flags, or provide evasion profiles.

faq.question: Which browser tools are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, and CDP-driven browsers when they expose the required page or debugging interface.

faq.question: Can the audit run without network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Offline mode runs the JavaScript-layer checks without the hosted network measurement.

faq.question: What does online mode send?
faq.answer: The documented hosted request can expose IP, ASN, HTTP, TLS, ClientHello, and request header metadata.

faq.question: How should results be used in CI?
faq.answer: Set a score threshold or fail on named bad checks, then review the failing signal before changing the browser configuration.
